title: The Mystery of Everyday Changes
intro: This quiz checks what you learned about physical and chemical changes — and how to tell them apart.

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between a physical change and a chemical change?
choices: Chemical changes form one or more new substances
questions.explanation: Chemical changes form one or more new substances, while physical changes do not.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a physical change?
questions.explanation: Melting ice is a physical change — water changes state but no new substance forms.

questions.prompt: Why is burning candle wax considered a chemical change?
choices: The wax changes from solid to liquid
New substances such as carbon dioxide and water vapor are formed
questions.explanation: Burning wax produces new substances such as carbon dioxide and water vapor.

questions.prompt: Why is rusting iron considered a chemical change?
choices: Iron reacts with oxygen and moisture to form new substances
The rust can be easily washed away
questions.explanation: Rusting is a chemical change because iron reacts with oxygen and moisture to form new substances.

questions.prompt: What is the most important question to ask when deciding whether a change is physical or chemical?
questions.explanation: Ask: Was a new substance formed? If yes, it is a chemical change; if no, it is a physical change.
